root_cause: Console.__init__ computed is_interactive only from force_interactive or (is_terminal and not is_dumb_terminal); unlike the sibling TTY_COMPATIBLE env var (tri-state in is_terminal: '0' forces False, '1' forces True, else auto-detect), there was no environment override for interactivity, so CI output that is TTY_COMPATIBLE still got spinners/progress animation and a non-tty file could not be forced interactive.
best_solution: In rich/console.py Console.__init__, just before `self.is_interactive = (...)`, add: if force_interactive is None, read `self._environ.get('TTY_INTERACTIVE')`; '0' -> force_interactive = False, '1' -> force_interactive = True, any other value leaves it None so auto-detection runs. The existing expression then applies it, keeping is_interactive a plain attribute and letting an explicit force_interactive argument win over the env var. Also add 'TTY_INTERACTIVE' to the env list in rich/diagnose.py (untested) and tidy the typing imports. Reasoning: the statement says it 'adds to the new TTY_COMPATIBLE', so grep TTY_COMPATIBLE, see its '0'/'1'/other tri-state, and mirror it for interactivity via the injectable self._environ.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that keeps is_interactive as the result of an '0'->False, '1'->True, otherwise-auto-detect override read from self._environ passes. v7 turned is_interactive into a read-only property that handles '0'/'1' and otherwise returns is_terminal. It passed, but it silently ignores the force_interactive argument and is_dumb_terminal, and it breaks code that assigns console.is_interactive. So it passed without being a faithful fix.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_console.py::test_tty_interactive: Console(file=io.BytesIO()) is not interactive; _environ={'TTY_INTERACTIVE':'1'} with BytesIO IS interactive (force True, even on a non-tty); _environ={'TTY_COMPATIBLE':'1'} is interactive; TTY_COMPATIBLE=1 plus TTY_INTERACTIVE=0 is constructed but has no assert; _environ={'TTY_INTERACTIVE':'foo'} falls back to auto-detect (not interactive). The env var must be read through the Console `_environ` kwarg, not os.environ.
locating_signals: The env var name TTY_INTERACTIVE and the phrase 'adds to the new TTY_COMPATIBLE' point to rich/console.py, where TTY_COMPATIBLE is handled in is_terminal and is_interactive is set in __init__. No function is named. Only the '=0' value is mentioned; the '=1' force-on case appears only in the hidden test.
our_outcome_summary: Passed: v7 only. v4 FAILED at tests/test_console.py:1050 (assert console.is_interactive with TTY_INTERACTIVE=1): its property only handled '0' and otherwise returned the stored auto-detected value, so '1' never forced True. It also added out-of-scope changes: it disabled Progress entirely when not interactive and changed Status auto_refresh. v6 FAILED at the same assertion: its one-line change added `tty_interactive != '0'` to the auto-detect expression and never handled '1'. v7 PASSED: a property mapping '0'->False, '1'->True, else is_terminal (it drops force_interactive and the dumb-terminal check) plus a Live auto_refresh tweak. v8 produced no patch: litellm ContextWindowExceededError (28,673 prompt tokens + 4,096 output > 32,768) after 26 tool calls and 145 LLM calls in 248 s.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement adds a setting (env var, flag, config key) described as a companion to an existing one, grep for the existing one and copy its full value semantics. Here that meant a tri-state '0' = force off, '1' = force on, anything else = auto-detect, even though the statement only mentioned the '0' case. Put the override where the existing value is resolved and before any explicit-argument default, so an explicit argument still wins. Read it through the object's injectable environment, since tests pass one in. Don't swap a public attribute for a read-only property, and don't change behavior in other modules (Progress, Live, Status) that the statement did not ask for.
